ghi_chu.mo_ta: The burning main building is a large church-like Gothic hall. It has a row of tall pinnacled spires, a traceried clerestory and a collapsing open-timber roof. It does not look like the Guildhall's real front.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The 1940 Guildhall had a medieval Gothic porch front and a flat-fronted hall. It had no row of tall spired buttresses like a cathedral, so the landmark is shown in the wrong form.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: A fire appliance with large spoked wheels and an open, carriage-like body stands in the street. It looks like a horse-drawn or very early motor pump.
ghi_chu.ly_do: By 1940 the London Fire Service (the wartime Auxiliary Fire Service and the National Fire Service) used motor pumps and trailer pumps. Spoked-wheel carriage appliances had been obsolete for decades.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: A street lamp is brightly lit. Several windows in the building on the right are also lit, and bright lights show among the crowd in the distance.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The wartime blackout was in force in London in December 1940, so street lamps and windows would have been unlit. Only the fire itself gave light.
